clue.text: It's OK to keep single and flourish

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something that is OK or acceptable is proper

explanation.surface: Staying unattached is fine, and it lets you thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, a direct synonym of flourish.

clue.text: Additional information given to Strasbourg party is false

parts.note: PS, postscript, adds information at the end of a letter
Strasbourg is a seat of the European Union, abbreviated EU
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A footnote is passed to a Strasbourg party, but it is untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham or not genuine, a synonym for false.

clue.text: It's not entirely reliable for a clear response

definitions.text: It's not entirely reliable for a clear response

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, the letters lying across them

explanation.surface: Something that cannot be relied upon to give a straight answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' signals the run of letters inside FOR A CLEAR; the whole clue also describes the Delphic prophet's famously ambiguous replies.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle gave prophetic responses that were often riddling and unreliable.

clue.text: Fastidious attitude of one city poser

indicators.note: made of, so the answer is formed out of these letters rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snooty urban show-off has a fussy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal is thin: 'of' as 'made of' has I CITY POSER rearranged; 'poser' hints at a puzzle to sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Preciosity is overrefinement or affected fastidiousness in manner or style.

clue.text: Sculptor given eroding material removed edges

indicators.note: taking off a word's edges leaves all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An artist works on stone that has worn away at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed edges' strips the first and last letters from ERODING.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: At the beginning of winter current goes off

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the month at the start of the northern winter
electric current is measured in amps

explanation.surface: As winter sets in, an electric current is switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, so decamps is a synonym of goes off.

clue.text: National flag — banner chewed and eaten by Fido

indicators.note: eaten by means taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a dog

indicators.note: chewed letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pet dog has chewed up and swallowed the national flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' is the anagram signal and 'eaten by' the container signal. The Dannebrog is Denmark's flag, a white cross on red.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dannebrog is the national flag of Denmark.

clue.text: Island unknown for being comfortable

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unidentified island is praised as snug.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy means warm and comfortable.

clue.text: Turn taken by model also known as a dish

indicators.note: taken by means absorbed into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous model
U, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: A model does a turn on the catwalk under an alias.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced meat.

clue.text: The usual ones are likely to be the first taken in

definitions.text: The usual ones are likely to be the first taken in

parts.words: The usual ones are likely to be the first taken in
parts.note: from the phrase rounding up the usual people police question; taken in means arrested

explanation.definitionFit: Suspects are the people police take in for questioning, the usual ones first.

clue.text: Growing out through having eaten junk

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it, here breaking the word up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's growth is blamed on eating junk food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' is the anagram signal on EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enate is a botanical term for something growing outward from a surface.

clue.text: Long dead creatures do Russian dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle into a new order

explanation.surface: Extinct animals are said to perform a Russian dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' is the anagram signal on DO RUSSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs are extinct reptiles that died out millions of years ago.

clue.text: Frivolous encounters make many marriages

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, standing for many
marriages are alliances between people or families

explanation.surface: Light flirtations can lead to lots of weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliances are casual, unserious romantic flings or flirtations.

clue.text: Backward English domestic slave in the past

definitions.text: Backward English domestic slave in the past

parts.words: Backward English domestic slave in the past
parts.note: backward English means English from far back in time, Anglo-Saxon, so this is a household bondsman of that era

explanation.surface: A slave of long ago who served an English household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' tempts a reversal, but here it means looking back in time, to Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: An esne was a labourer or household slave in Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: Ocean hazard is the chief object

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
hazard means chance or risk

explanation.surface: The danger of the sea is the most important thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The main chance is one's own chief interest or advantage, an idiom.

clue.text: Rump steak? Er, not exactly where to get it

indicators.note: not exactly as written, so the letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over buying rump steak, wondering where to find it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not exactly' is the anagram signal on RUMP STEAK ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket is a large food shop where one could buy steak.

clue.text: Write up resort shortly as a magic figure

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Margate is a seaside resort in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone writes a quick account of a holiday town, as a magic sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the resort's last letter and 'up' reverses what is left, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star used as a magical or occult symbol.

clue.text: So-called cow's liver, perhaps

parts.note: a liver here is one who lives somewhere: Jersey and Guernsey cows are named after islands, so a resident there

explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Jersey or Guernsey lives on an island that gives a cow breed its name.

clue.text: With it one isn't

parts.note: with it in the sense of conscious: under this condition a person is not

explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a state of stupor induced by drugs, so one is not alert.

clue.text: Gee — and they're off with a bang!

parts.note: the letter G, spelt as a word, is the opening letter of the word gun

explanation.surface: A racing commentator's cry as the race begins with a loud report.
explanation.walkthrough: Read STARTING GUN as 'the starting letter of GUN': that is G, and 'Gee' is how G is spelt as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting gun is fired to set runners off at the beginning of a race.

clue.text: Caution about taking a long time on the Internet

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the joined pieces read backwards

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
the web is the Internet

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful about spending ages online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ERAWEB round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is a warning to take care, used as an imperative of caution.

clue.text: River takes the lid off a hot place

indicators.note: removing the lid of a word in a down clue drops its top, first letter

parts.note: a kitchen is a hot place where cooking happens

explanation.surface: Someone lifts the lid off a pan in a warm room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the lid off' removes the K from KITCHEN. The Itchen is a river in Hampshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Itchen is a chalk-stream river flowing through Winchester and Southampton.

clue.text: Principal feature of a leading Roman church

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is its first one

explanation.surface: Something characteristic of a major church in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature of' just links the definition to the wordplay; the surface hints at the architectural arch, a fitting extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief, as in arch-enemy or archbishop.

clue.text: Article is sent to the Queen in case of criminal deportation

indicators.note: to be put in the case of something is to be enclosed inside it

parts.note: bent is slang for criminal or corrupt
an is the indefinite article
taken as written
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A piece of writing goes to the monarch about a criminal deportation case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case of' is the container signal; 'sent to' only sets the Queen after the article and 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment is being sent away or expelled from a country, much like deportation.

clue.text: Least active student sent down %u2014 that is …

indicators.note: a student sent down is expelled from university, so the letter is removed

parts.note: idlest means the least active
L stands for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: The laziest student is expelled, which is to say...
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

clue.text: … one reportedly active, but unforthcoming

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: one active, a person who does things, is a doer

explanation.surface: Someone said to be busy is nonetheless taciturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' joins 'active' to make a doer, which said aloud sounds like DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour means stern and gloomy, so not forthcoming or communicative.

clue.text: Speech to put off by replacing silver with a bit of it

indicators.note: replacing one thing with another means swapping letters in the word

parts.note: to discourage someone is to put them off
AG is the chemical symbol for silver
it refers back to silver, and a bit of that word is its first letter, S

explanation.surface: An instruction on dissuading someone by substituting some of the silver.
explanation.walkthrough: In DISCOURAGE the AG becomes S, the first letter of silver, to which 'it' points back.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is a formal spoken or written discussion, so it is a synonym for a speech.

clue.text: In South Wales, down under

definitions.meaning: a town in Glamorgan, south Wales
a poetic shortening of beneath, meaning below or under

explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a Welsh town, and 'neath is the poetic clipped form of beneath.

clue.text: The beak, whence comes 25 …

definitions.meaning: in zoology a bird's beak or snout-like projection has this Latin name
the platform a speaker stands on to deliver a speech, the answer to 25

explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is both an animal's beak in biology and a raised platform for public speaking.

clue.text: … in which is the means of control

parts.note: taken as written
a rein is a strap used to control a horse

explanation.surface: Inside it lies the way to keep control.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning in that place or in which.
